business.what_it_does: Scheduling infrastructure that lets an individual or a team create bookable event types, capture client info through routing forms that assign the right consultant or coach automatically, and manage bookings, workflows and calendars via a self-serve product or a public API — deployable cloud, self-hosted, or open-source.
business.business_model: Freemium subscription: a free individual tier, paid per-user/month plans for Teams and Organizations (billed yearly with a stated 25% discount), and custom enterprise pricing sold through sales; smaller add-on subscriptions (e.g. premium usernames) exist alongside it.

facts.statement: The Free plan is free forever, capped at 1 user, with no usage limits on event types and calendars.

provenance.quote: Start scheduling for free, with no usage limits.

facts.statement: The Teams plan is listed at $12 per user/month on yearly billing, described as a 25% saving over monthly.

provenance.quote:
### Teams
YEARLY

### $12
per user/month

Save 25%

facts.statement: The FAQ page separately states a team account costs $15 per month for each team member — this does not match the $12/user/month figure shown on the pricing page (likely the un-discounted monthly rate vs. the yearly rate), and the two should not be silently merged.

provenance.quote: A team account costs $15 per month for each team member.

facts.statement: The Organizations plan is listed at $28 per user/month on yearly billing, also described as a 25% saving.

provenance.quote:
### Organizations
YEARLY

### $28
per user/month

Save 25%

facts.statement: Both Teams and Organizations plans are sold with a 14-day free trial.

provenance.quote: *14 day free trial

facts.statement: The top (Custom/Enterprise) plan has no published price and is sold via sales conversation.

provenance.quote:
### Custom
The most advanced scheduling for enterprise without limits.

[Talk to sales]

facts.statement: The API supports three authentication methods: OAuth, API key, and a deprecated Platform method.

provenance.source: Introduction to API v2 - Cal.com Docs
provenance.quote:
The Cal.com API has 3 authentication methods:

1. OAuth
2. API key
3. Platform (Deprecated)

facts.statement: The default/API-key rate limit is 120 requests per minute, with higher limits available and, above a point, extra charges.

provenance.source: Introduction to API v2 - Cal.com Docs
provenance.quote: API Key - 120 requests per minute. This can be increased to a reasonable amount, such as 200 requests per minute. If you require a higher rate limit, such as 800 requests per minute, it is possible, but it may involve extra charges.

facts.statement: As of 15 December 2025, Cal.com stopped accepting new signups for its 'Platform' offering, continuing support only for existing customers.

provenance.source: Introduction to API v2 - Cal.com Docs
provenance.quote: As of 15th December 2025, we're currently undergoing a restructuring of our "Platform"-offering... we continue to provide enterprise support for existing customers but no longer offer new signups for any "Platform" plan.

facts.statement: The product carries ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA and GDPR compliance, plus EU-US Data Privacy Framework and HIPAA certifications.

provenance.quote: Our product is ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA, and GDPR compliant. In addition, we also have EU-US Data Privacy Framework and HIPAA certifications.

facts.statement: A premium/reserved username can be rented as a $29/month add-on subscription.

provenance.quote: you will be prompted to upgrade to premium for $29 a month.

facts.statement: Cal.com positions itself against Calendly by noting Calendly paywalls features (monetization, analytics, advanced customization) that Cal.com gives away free to individuals.

provenance.quote: Calendly's paid plan is comparable to what Cal.com offers for free to individuals. Our free plan includes essential features like unlimited event types and calendars, plus powerful capabilities—such as monetization, analytics, and advanced customization—that Calendly places behind a paywall.

facts.statement: The product can be deployed open-source, self-hosted, or cloud-hosted, and this flexibility is marketed specifically to consulting and coaching teams for compliance and customization reasons.

provenance.source: Effortless Scheduling And Smart Routing For Consulting And Coaching Teams | Cal.com
provenance.quote: Choose open-source, self-hosted, or cloud deployment to meet your organization's unique security and customization needs.

facts.statement: A live booking page (e.g. Lucas Chu's) shows the product's core unit is the named, duration-based 'event type' (examples seen: Secret Meeting 15m, 25 Min Meeting, 15 Min Meeting via Zoom) that visitors book directly.

provenance.quote:
## Secret Meeting

- 15m

## 25 Min Meeting

- 25m

## 15 Min Meeting

- 15m

facts.statement: Cal.com is used by consulting and coaching businesses specifically to qualify prospective clients before a call and route them to the best-fit consultant or coach automatically.

Because pricing, trials, and 'Get started' signup links are shown directly on the marketing site, the product is primarily self-serve for individuals and small teams, with sales conversations reserved for the top (Custom) tier.

entries.claim: Cal.com's mission is to connect a billion people by 2031 through calendar scheduling.
entries.verbatim: Our mission is to connect a billion people by 2031 through calendar scheduling.

entries.claim: Cal.com and Cal are registered trademarks of Cal.com, Inc.
entries.verbatim: Cal.com® and Cal® are registered trademarks of Cal.com, Inc. All rights reserved.

entries.claim: Cal.com's free plan includes unlimited event types and calendars, plus monetization, analytics, and advanced customization that Calendly places behind a paywall
entries.verbatim: Our free plan includes essential features like unlimited event types and calendars, plus powerful capabilities—such as monetization, analytics, and advanced customization—that Calendly places behind a paywall.

entries.claim: For teams and organizations, Cal.com offers enterprise-ready features like full admin controls, org-wide scheduling, advanced routing, and deeper branding and compliance support
entries.verbatim: For teams and organizations, Cal.com also goes further with enterprise-ready features like full admin controls, org-wide scheduling, advanced routing, and deeper branding and compliance support.

entries.claim: Individual accounts on Cal.com are free
entries.verbatim: The first thing you need to know is that while individual accounts are free, team accounts are not.

entries.claim: A team account costs $15 per month per team member
entries.verbatim: A team account costs $15 per month for each team member.

entries.claim: Team accounts include managed meeting templates, collective events, and round-robin scheduling
entries.verbatim: These features include things like managed meeting templates, collective events, and round-robin scheduling.

entries.claim: Upgrading to a premium username costs $29 a month
entries.verbatim: Once you enter the premium name in the username field and click update, you will be prompted to upgrade to premium for $29 a month.

entries.claim: Cal.com's product is ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA, and GDPR compliant
entries.verbatim: Our product is ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA, and GDPR compliant.

entries.claim: Cal.com has EU-US Data Privacy Framework and HIPAA certifications
entries.verbatim: In addition, we also have EU-US Data Privacy Framework and HIPAA certifications.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers white-labeling options
entries.verbatim: Yes, Cal.com does offer white-labeling options.

entries.claim: Cal.com users can have as many calendar connections as they want, with no limit imposed
entries.verbatim: Cal.com users can have as many calendar connections as they would like. If you want to have one calendar connection, that's fine, but you can also have twelve if that's what works for you.

entries.claim: Cal.com supports date overrides, letting users specify one-off schedule changes such as different working days for a set period without creating a new schedule
entries.verbatim: Date overrides are a feature that lets you add one-off adjustments to an availability schedule. This is useful when you know that your schedule might be different for a week or two but you don't want to create a brand new schedule just because of that.

entries.claim: Cal.com's routing forms ask visitors questions and direct them to the bookable event that most closely matches their needs
entries.verbatim: Routing forms will ask the visitor a series of questions and then, based on their answers, direct them to the bookable event that most closely matches their needs.

entries.claim: Organizations with 30 or more members are recommended to use an enterprise plan rather than a team subscription
entries.verbatim: If you're an organization with 30 or more members and value customization as well as white labeling, then you're probably going to need an enterprise license as opposed to a team subscription.

entries.claim: Enterprise licenses come with advanced options for security and are typically chosen by organizations in human resources, healthcare, education, legal, and government-adjacent fields
entries.verbatim: Enterprise licenses come with advanced options for security and are typically chosen by professionals and organizations working within human resources, healthcare, education, legal, and government adjacent fields.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers multiple payment options including credit card and bank transfer, and absorbs the associated fees
entries.verbatim: We have multiple payment options, credit card, bank transfer, etc. We absorb the fees.

entries.claim: Free Cal.com users have access to over 90% of all the platform's features
entries.verbatim: Free Cal.com users have access to over 90% of all our features.

entries.claim: Free accounts include unlimited events, opt-in meetings, multiple availability schedules, unlimited calendar integrations, recurring events, monetization, analytics, third-party integrations, webhooks, automated workflows, and routing forms
entries.verbatim: These include things like unlimited events, opt-in meetings, multiple availability schedules, unlimited calendars integration, recurring events, monetization, analytics, third-party integrations, webhooks, automated workflows, routing forms, and a whole lot more.

entries.claim: Removing Cal.com's branding from the booking interface requires signing up for a team plan, which can consist of a single individual
entries.verbatim: If you'd like to remove Cal.com's logo and related branding from your booking interface, you'll want to sign up for a team plan. Luckily, a team doesn't have to be more than a single individual.

entries.claim: Products built with Cal.com's open-source code must themselves remain open source under the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) Version 3
entries.verbatim: This is because Cal.com is published under the GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL), Version 3.

entries.claim: Users cannot rebrand and republish the enterprise edition (/ee/) of Cal.com without purchasing a license and permission
entries.verbatim: One limitation is, that you cannot rebrand and republish the enterprise edition (/ee/) without purchasing a license and permission.

entries.claim: Cal.com cross-references your calendars in order to understand when you are available for bookings
entries.verbatim: Cal.com acts as a hub and a point of coordination for your connected calendars. This means that Cal.com cross-references your calendars in order to understand when you are available for bookings.

entries.claim: Cancelling an event on a connected calendar does not automatically remove the appointment from the booking section of your Cal.com dashboard
entries.verbatim: If you cancel an event that’s been added to your calendar, that will not automatically remove the appointment from the booking section of your Cal.com dashboard.

entries.claim: Cal Video offers real-time transcription, screen recording sent to your email, instant meetings, and dial-in support
entries.verbatim: Cal Video offers high-quality service with features such as real-time transcription, screen recording sent to your email, instant meetings, and dial-in support for seamless communication.

entries.claim: Cal.ai is Cal.com's AI voice assistant used for outbound calls to schedule meetings, follow up on missing documents, or send reminders about upcoming appointments
entries.verbatim: Cal.ai is our AI voice assistant used for outbound calls to schedule meetings, follow up on missing documents, or send reminders about upcoming appointments.

entries.claim: Cal.com users can have as many calendar connections as they would like, with no limit
entries.verbatim: Cal.com users can have as many calendar connections as they would like. If you want to have one calendar connection, that's fine, but you can also have twelve if that's what works for you.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers a pre-made Apple Calendar integration available in the Cal.com App Store
entries.verbatim: You have a variety of options when adding calendars, however the easiest way to add an Apple calendar is probably just to use our pre-made integration which can be found in the Cal.com App Store.

entries.claim: Users can create paid events such as one-on-one coaching and consulting sessions, as well as mentor check-ins
entries.verbatim: For example, you can create paid events like one-on-one coaching and consulting sessions, as well as check-ins with a mentor.

entries.claim: Users can create group events like open houses, masterclasses, workshops, or webinars
entries.verbatim: You can also create group events like open houses, masterclasses, workshops, or webinars.

entries.claim: Events can happen in-person, remote, or over the phone
entries.verbatim: The events you create can happen in-person, remote, or over the phone.

entries.claim: Users can create hidden events that require a shared link to book
entries.verbatim: You can create hidden events that people need you to send them a link to if they'd like to book it.

entries.claim: Users can create events with private single-use booking links
entries.verbatim: You can also create events with private single-use booking links.

entries.claim: Users can create opt-in events where the host must confirm each booking request before it is finalized
entries.verbatim: You can create opt-in events, meaning that when someone requests to attend that event, you have to confirm that you accept that request before the event is finalized.

entries.claim: Every Cal.com user has a profile link in the format Cal.com/your username that lets others book based on availability without a fixed date or time
entries.verbatim: However, every Cal.com user has a profile link in addition to individual event links. Your profile link is Cal.com/your username.

entries.claim: Events can be toggled between public (shown on the public profile) and private (bookable only via direct link)
entries.verbatim: All Cal.com users have the ability to create private events. The only difference between a private event and a regular event is that a private event isn't going to be displayed on your public profile.

entries.claim: Private links anonymize the user's Cal.com information and are single-use, regenerating after each use
entries.verbatim: Private links work by anonymizing your Cal.com user information. All private links are single-use and regenerate after they are used.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers a seats feature that allows multiple bookings for a single time slot, useful for group classes, open houses, and orientation sessions
entries.verbatim: You can offer multiple bookings for a single event in a single time slot by using our seats feature. This is great if you want to offer things like group classes, open houses, and orientation sessions.

entries.claim: There is no limit to the number of availability schedules a user can create
entries.verbatim: There are no limits to the number of availability schedules you can have. You can create 10, 20, or 100 - it's up to you.

entries.claim: A user can only have one default availability schedule at any given time, though it can be changed anytime
entries.verbatim: Just so you know, you can only have one default availability schedule at any given time, however, you can also change it whenever you want.

entries.claim: Cal.com supports a wide variety of in-person and virtual locations, including office, phone, teleconferencing platforms, Telegram, and Signal
entries.verbatim: Cal.com supports a wide variety of in-person and virtual locations. This means that a meeting location can be set to be at a specific venue like an office, over the phone, via a teleconferencing platform, or it could happen on Telegram or Signal.

entries.claim: An event can have more than one location, and the attendee chooses which location to use when booking
entries.verbatim: The plus button right below the location drop-down menu lets you add additional locations to your Cal.com event. One thing you have to remember, though, is that when you have more than one location, it means that the attendee is ultimately choosing where the meeting is going to happen.

entries.claim: Users can add an additional email to their Cal.com profile and designate it as the email shown in booking confirmations, either as primary or at the event level
entries.verbatim: You will notice that there is a button marked [+ add email]. Clicking on this will let you add an additional email to your Cal.com profile. This email can then be made your primary email and you can also designate it as the email that information is sent to within your event-level settings.

entries.claim: Cal.com places no limit on the number of workflows you can create or the number of events you can connect them to.
entries.verbatim: There is no limit on the number of workflows you can create or the number of events you can connect them to.

entries.claim: Cal.com's buffer time setting ensures 5 to 10 minutes between meetings.
entries.verbatim: A buffer time helps ensure that you always have 5 to 10 minutes between meetings.

entries.claim: Cal.com integrates with Stripe to let users monetize their meetings.
entries.verbatim: You can monetize your meetings thanks to our integration with Stripe.

entries.claim: Cal.com integrates with Zoom to host meetings, but meetings longer than 45 minutes require a paid Zoom account.
entries.verbatim: A great example of this is Zoom. Once you install our integration for Zoom, you can use the platform to host your meetings. However, if you want a meeting that's longer than 45 minutes, then Zoom will require you to have a paid Zoom account.

entries.claim: Cal.com does not currently have a mobile app for Android or iPhone; it can be used on mobile through a browser.
entries.verbatim: At the moment we do not have a mobile app. If you would like to use cal.com on your mobile, you can do this through your browser.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers a desktop app, though it does not provide the exact same experience as the browser-based product and is updated less frequently.
entries.verbatim: However, we do have a desktop app as well. It should be noted that the desktop app does not provide the exact same experience as what you may be used to when using Cal.com via your browser.

entries.claim: CalVideo, Cal.com's in-house video conferencing platform, is powered by Daily.co.
entries.verbatim: CalVideo is our in-house video conferencing platform powered by Daily.co.

entries.claim: CalVideo supports 1-on-1 meetings and group events, is low latency, white-label-friendly, and offers optional features like screen recording depending on subscription type.
entries.verbatim: You can use CalVideo to host 1-on-1 meetings as well as group events. CalVideo is also low latency, white label-friendly, and, depending on your subscription type, comes with optional features like screen recording.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers a WordPress plugin as the easiest way to add a booking page to a WordPress site.
entries.verbatim: For many people, however, the easiest way to add a Cal.com booking page to the WordPress site is by using our plugin for WordPress.

entries.claim: The majority of apps in Cal.com's app store are free to install, though some require a paid account with the third-party service to access all features.
entries.verbatim: The majority of the apps in the store can be installed for free. However, some of them do require a paid account with another service to access all their features.

entries.claim: Signing up for a Teams subscription starts with creating a free Cal.com account.
entries.verbatim: You can sign up for a Teams account by first signing up for a free Cal.com account.

entries.claim: Declining a Cal.com invite via Gmail's Yes/No/Maybe buttons does not cancel or change the underlying Cal.com booking.
entries.verbatim: If someone receives an invitation to a Cal.com event and they decline it using Gmail's Yes, No, or Maybe buttons, you will be able to see that via your Gmail interface and the attendance information on your connected Google Calendar. However, that will not cancel or change the Cal.com booking itself.

entries.claim: Cal.com's routing forms ask visitors a series of questions and route them to the bookable event that best matches their answers.
entries.verbatim: Routing forms will ask the visitor a series of questions and then, based on their answers, direct them to the bookable event that most closely matches their needs.

entries.claim: Cal.com's dynamic booking links only show time slots when all parties are mutually available.
entries.verbatim: The great thing about this page is that all the time slots that appear are only those in which all parties are mutually available.

entries.claim: Enabling opt-in bookings requires host approval before a meeting is finalized, and the host receives an email notification whenever a meeting is requested.
entries.verbatim: Turning this setting on means that you get to approve prospective meetings before they're added to your calendar. After you've enabled this option, you’ll receive an email at your registered email address whenever a meeting is requested.

entries.claim: Cal.com's booking limits include buffer times, duration limits, and frequency limits, among others.
entries.verbatim: These limits include things like buffer times, as well as duration, frequency, and more.

entries.claim: Cal.com's inline embed matches the booking interface's spacing and margins to the rest of the website.
entries.verbatim: An inline embed is the ideal option if you want to ensure that your booking interface utilizes the same spacing and margins as the rest of the items on your website.

entries.claim: Cal.com's popup embed generates a customizable booking button that opens a calendar when clicked.
entries.verbatim: Cal.com's popup embed generates a booking button that, when clicked, opens up a calendar that guests can use to book appointments.

entries.claim: Cal.com's popup via element click embed opens a booking calendar when a user clicks anywhere on the website page.
entries.verbatim: This option is a combination of the inline embed and the popup button. Once a user clicks somewhere on your website page, a booking calendar will appear.

entries.claim: Cal.com offers an email embed option that simplifies sharing a calendar link via a graphic element with links and text.
entries.verbatim: The final embed option that we offer is made for emails. Basically, it simplifies sharing/explaining how a calendar link works.

entries.claim: Cal.com's app store is a repository of third-party integrations covering analytics, teleconferencing platforms, payment gateways, and more.
entries.verbatim: Cal.com's app store is a repository for all of our third-party integrations. You can use the app store to add everything from analytics to teleconferencing platforms, payment gateways, and more.

entries.claim: Cal.com's booking form (booking questions) asks bookers for information such as name, phone number, and meeting purpose.
entries.verbatim: Whenever someone books an appointment with you, there's a little form they have to fill out. It'll ask them questions like their name, their phone number, or what the meeting's about.

entries.claim: CalVideo meetings don't automatically end or time out after 45 minutes and can be as long or short as needed
entries.verbatim: One of the benefits of using CalVideo is that you don't have to worry about your meeting automatically ending or timing out after 45 minutes. Meetings conducted via CalVideo can be as long or short as you'd like.

voice.person: Mostly "we/our" as the company, with the product referred to by name ("Cal.com offers...") in marketing copy; documentation slips into direct address ("you can view...").

segments.name: The dev-tool founder whose Calendly link is the worst-designed surface he ships
segments.situation: He runs or co-founds a small technical company, or sells his own expertise as a named individual, and his booking link is public infrastructure: email signature, site footer, conference bio, DM replies. Every other surface he ships he controls down to the font; the booking page is the one place a competitor's logo sits on his brand. He is already paying for a scheduling tool and uses a small fraction of it. When he last tried to change something — a duration, an event's details — he went looking in the dashboard and could not find it; Ant Wilson of Supabase says publicly that this is exactly what finally moved him. His peer group has already gone: Kent C. Dodds migrated, Guillermo Rauch at Vercel, Aria Minaei at Theatre.JS, Flo Merian at Mintlify all use it and say so by name. He is not researching a category. He is deciding whether this week is the week he changes the link.

segments.name: The partner in a small consulting or coaching practice where every enquiry lands on whoever answers email first
segments.situation: Two to six practitioners share the client list and the specialisms are not interchangeable — one does the regulated-industry work, one coaches founders, one works in a second language. The booking link is generic, so a client picks a slot and the practice finds out what the session is actually about when the call starts. The first ten minutes of paid or pre-sales time go on questions that could have been asked in a form, and sometimes the call ends with 'you should really speak to my colleague', which means rebooking and a client who has now told their story twice. Intake currently happens as email back-and-forth before a time is agreed, or not at all. Cal.com markets to exactly this practice: it says teams like this use routing forms to qualify leads, guide them to the right service, and assign clients by expertise, language, location or availability. Whether these practices actually behave this way is the vendor's assertion, not something observed here.

objections.objection: We already run on Calendly. The link is in email signatures, on the website, in job posts and in people's bios — switching means chasing every place it lives and breaking any of them I miss.
objections.answer: Cal.com offers 1-click import of Calendly events (E132), so the event types themselves do not have to be rebuilt, and the free plan is free forever with no usage limits (E39, E126), so the migration can be run in parallel before anything is cut over. A named peer states publicly that he simply migrated (E31). Note the limit: the evidence covers importing events into Cal.com, not finding and rewriting the existing links, embeds and signatures — nothing in the ledger addresses that part of the work.

objections.objection: Your pricing page says $12 per user/month and your own FAQ says a team account costs $15 per member. If I cannot trust the price on the page, what else on it is stale?
objections.answer: Nothing in the supplied evidence reconciles these. The pricing page states $12 per user/month on yearly billing described as a 25% saving (E133), and the FAQ separately states $15 per month per team member (E40). The likely explanation is monthly versus discounted-yearly, but no supplied source says so, and the copy must not assert it. This objection cannot be answered with what we currently know; the safe move is to quote one figure with its billing term attached and never present the two as one price.

objections.objection: I am one person. Paying a per-user 'team' price so that your logo comes off my booking page reads as a hostage fee, not a plan.
objections.answer: Cal.com's own help docs state that a team does not have to be more than a single individual (E54, E107), and that the upgrade also brings collective events, round-robin and CalVideo recording rather than only branding removal (E108, E101). The free tier is otherwise unusually complete — Cal.com claims free users get over 90% of all features (E52, E53). What the evidence does not do is make the logo removal itself feel worth a recurring per-user bill; the honest framing is that branding is a side-effect of the team tier, not its pitch.

objections.objection: You stopped taking new signups for the Platform product in December 2025. Why would I build my product's booking layer on a company that just closed the thing I would be buying?
objections.answer: Only partially answerable. Cal.com states that as of 15 December 2025 it no longer offers new signups for any Platform plan and continues enterprise support for existing customers only (E118) — there is no replacement path in the evidence for a new platform customer, and that is the finding. What survives for a builder is the ordinary API: Teams customers get every endpoint except Platform- and Orgs-prefixed ones (E119), Organizations customers get everything except Platform, Teams and Orgs/Orgs (E120), with OAuth and API-key auth (E111) and Custom APIs listed in the Teams plan. Anyone needing managed users specifically should not be written to as a prospect.

objections.objection: 'Open source' means AGPL. If we self-host and touch the code, our own product has to be open too — that is a legal problem, not a feature.
objections.answer: The concern is correct as stated and the evidence confirms it: Cal.com is published under AGPL v3 and products built with its code must themselves remain open source (E55), and the enterprise edition cannot be rebranded and republished without a purchased licence (E56). The resolutions in the evidence are commercial, not legal reassurance: an enterprise self-hosting licence is obtained through sales (E106), and cloud deployment avoids the question entirely while keeping the same product (E2, E15). Do not sell 'open source' to a buyer who has not asked for it.

objections.objection: We handle patient or client data. Adding a scheduling vendor adds a place that data can leak, and I will have to defend that choice to an auditor.
objections.answer: This is the best-evidenced objection in the set. The product is ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CCPA and GDPR compliant (E43, E178) with EU-US Data Privacy Framework and HIPAA certifications (E44), supports HIPAA requirements for handling PHI (E173), offers US and EU hosting (E179), a dedicated database environment on the top tier (E180, E158), SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning (E148, E175, E176), role-based permissions (E152, E174), and — if hosting the vendor at all is the objection — self-hosted or open-source deployment giving full control over client data and infrastructure (E3, E2). A named buyer in health has already made this argument publicly (E25).

provenance.source: Cal.com testimonial — Micah Friedland, CEO & Founder, Navi
provenance.quote: At Navi, protecting personal health information is a non-negotiable, so choosing Cal.com for scheduling just makes sense.

objections.objection: It is open source and the free tier does almost everything. We can self-host it, or wire up a booking page ourselves, and pay nothing.
objections.answer: Nothing in the evidence closes this, and Cal.com's own claims arguably open it: free users are said to have access to over 90% of all features (E52, E53) and self-hosting is offered outright (E3). There is no case study, no maintenance cost and no customer statement in the ledger about anyone who self-hosted and regretted it. The only counterweights available are that a self-build inherits none of the certifications (E43, E44, E178), none of the 100+ direct integrations and calendar/conferencing sync (E193, E181, E183, E131), and none of the routing and round-robin logic (E159, E11) — and that the paid tiers exist for collaboration features a single-user build does not have (E135, E137). Treat this as unbeaten for technically capable buyers.

objections.objection: Routing forms and round-robin are for sales floors with a pool of reps. There are three of us and we know who takes what.
objections.answer: Partly answerable, and the evidence is inconsistent here, which is worth knowing. Cal.com's help docs list routing forms among free-account features (E53) while the pricing page lists routing forms under the Teams plan (E141) — do not assert either as the reader's entitlement. What is safe: a team can be a single individual (E54), the no-code form builder is pitched at small practices whose offerings change (E10), and the value framed for them is qualification before the call rather than distribution across a rep pool (E12, E8). The 14-day trial (E134) lets them test it without an argument about size.

objections.objection: Your pricing page sells a Mobile App and your own help docs say you do not have one. Which is it?
objections.answer: Unresolved in the evidence. The Free plan feature list includes 'Mobile App' and browser extensions for managing bookings on the go (E129, E190), while the help documentation states there is currently no mobile app for Android or iPhone and directs users to a browser (E82), adding that a desktop app exists but does not provide the same experience and is updated less often (E83). Do not promise a mobile app in copy.

objections.objection: 120 requests a minute will not carry our booking volume, and you have already told me more costs extra without telling me how much.
objections.answer: Only partly answerable. The documented default and API-key limit is 120 requests per minute (E114, E117), which can be raised to a reasonable amount such as 200 (E115); a higher limit such as 800 is possible but may involve extra charges (E116) and no price is published for it. Anything beyond that is a sales conversation on the Custom tier (E154, E155). For a reader whose objection is volume economics, the evidence gives a number and a shrug — say so rather than implying the ceiling is negotiable.

notes: 6 of 200 candidate fact(s) were discarded because the quote supporting them could not be found in the source.
